newsitem.title: CHINA: HK PROPERTY STOCKS DOWN ON MORTGAGE RATE HIKE.
newsitem.headline: HK PROPERTY STOCKS DOWN ON MORTGAGE RATE HIKE.

text.p: A rise in mortgage lending rates at some Hong Kong banks pushed property stocks lower on Tuesday with investors fearing that the banks' move would dampen home buyers' interest in purchasing flats, brokers said.
"A rise in mortgage rates by a major bank fuelled expectations that other smaller banks would follow. It will affect the property market," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
"Investors are taking the mortgage rate hike as an opportunity to take profit after the recent rally in the sector," he added.
Hongkong Bank and Standard Chartered Bank recently raised their mortgage rates by 25 basis points to 9.25 percent.
Shares of Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, which topped the net losers list, fell HK$1.50 or 1.47 percent, to HK$100.50 in late morning trade.
It was followed by Great Eagle Holdings Ltd, which fell HK$0.75, or 2.65 percent, to HK$27.50.
Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd eased HK$0.50 to HK$93.25, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was down HK$0.50 to HK$71 and Hysan Development Co Ltd eased HK$0.20 to HK$26.30.
Brokers said they expected the property counters to consolidate after the pullback.
